applicableAreas: Detention pond in northeast corner adjacent to overhead electric line on eastern property boundary
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows biofiltration/detention pond located in the northeast corner of the site adjacent to the eastern property boundary. Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) confirms an overhead electric line labeled '-OE-' running north-south along the eastern property boundary, positioned directly adjacent to the pond wall. Sheet 15 shows the pond plan details with rim elevation 681.00' and water surface elevations ranging from 676.25' to 676.75' for various storm events. Sheet 16 shows pond section profiles with detailed elevations but does NOT include elevation views or cross-sections showing the horizontal distance or clearance from the overhead conductors to the pond edge. No engineer-sealed profile exhibits demonstrating the 7-foot-6-inch minimum sky-to-ground clearance were found.
findings.reasoning: The detention pond is a man-made water quality feature (defined as a water quality feature under the checklist). The overhead electric line running along the eastern boundary serves distribution facilities (indicated by '-OE-' notation and transformer pads shown on Sheet 21, confirming distribution voltage, not transmission). UCM § 1.10.3 requires a minimum 7-foot-6-inch horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the pond edge to the nearest overhead distribution conductor. The site plan documents do not provide evidence of this clearance: Sheet 16's pond profiles show only the pond's internal cross-sections and elevation changes, not the clearance to the adjacent overhead line. No dimension lines, callouts, or professional engineer certification showing the measured distance between the pond boundary and the overhead conductors are present in the submitted plans. The absence of this clearance verification documentation, combined with the pond's adjacency to the overhead line, indicates non-compliance with the requirement.
findings.comment: Biofiltration/detention pond in the northeast corner is adjacent to overhead distribution electric line on eastern property boundary. No engineer-sealed profile or section exhibits demonstrate the required minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from conductors to pond edge. Provide profile sheets showing measured horizontal clearance from outermost conductor to nearest pond edge, with professional engineer seal confirming minimum 7.5-foot clearance per UCM § 1.10.3.

applicableAreas: Detention pond in northeast corner relative to overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors
findings.observation: Sheet 9 shows the detention pond in the northeast corner adjacent to the eastern property boundary. Sheet 12 shows the overhead electric line (-OE-) running along that boundary in close proximity to the pond wall. Sheet 15 and 16 provide pond details and profiles but do NOT include radial clearance exhibits showing distances from the overhead primary and neutral conductors to the pond edge measured in all directions (north, south, east, west from the conductors). No engineer certification or dimension callouts showing the 15-foot radial clearance are present.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires water quality features to maintain a minimum 15-foot radial clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors, measured as a radius in all directions from the conductor locations. The detention pond's proximity to the overhead line on the eastern boundary suggests potential non-compliance. The submitted plans do not provide professional engineer-sealed exhibits demonstrating that the pond maintains this 15-foot radial clearance. Without such documentation, the application cannot demonstrate compliance. The presence of the pond adjacent to the overhead line, without radial clearance verification, indicates a deficiency.
findings.comment: Detention pond does not demonstrate required minimum 15-foot radial clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. Provide engineer-sealed radial clearance exhibits showing distances from conductor locations to pond edge measured in all directions, with professional engineer certification confirming minimum 15-foot radial clearance per UCM § 1.10.3.

applicableAreas: Detention pond near overhead electric facilities in northeast corner
findings.observation: The detention pond is positioned within 15 feet of overhead electric conductors on the eastern property boundary (confirmed by Sheet 9 showing pond position and Sheet 12 showing overhead line location). Sheets 15 and 16 contain pond design cross-sections and profiles showing internal pond elevations and sedimentation/filtration details. However, these sheets do not include professional engineer-sealed profile sections or elevation views that show: (1) the location of the overhead conductors (all phases), (2) the exact location of the pond boundary, and (3) the horizontal and vertical clearances between the pond edge and the nearest conductor with dimension callouts. No detail sections referenced in the drainage plan sheets (Sheets 15-16) are cross-referenced to sheets showing this clearance verification.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires that where water quality features are proposed near electric facilities (within 15 feet of overhead conductors), plans must include profile plans, engineer-scaled section exhibits, or elevation views showing clearance verification with dimensions between water quality features and electric facilities. The requirement is explicit: applicants must demonstrate compliance through professional engineer-certified exhibits showing measured clearances. The pond profiles provided (Sheets 16 Sections A-A and B-B) show pond geometry and internal elevations but do not extend to show the overhead conductors or clearance dimensions. This deficiency requires submission of additional exhibit sheets showing the clearance verification.
findings.comment: Missing engineer-sealed profile plans or section exhibits showing clearance verification and dimensions between detention pond and overhead electric conductors. Submit professional engineer-prepared profiles showing conductor locations (all phases), pond boundary location, and horizontal/vertical clearances with dimension callouts demonstrating compliance with UCM § 1.10.3 minimum clearances (7.5 feet horizontal, 15 feet radial).

applicableAreas: Tree plantings within 5-foot electric easements on northern, eastern, and southern property boundaries
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows tree plantings (marked with symbols including 'M' for mitigation trees, 'SY' for street yard trees, 'PL' for parking lot trees) positioned directly adjacent to and overlapping the property boundary lines on the north, south, and east sides of the site. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts 5-foot electric easements running along these same property boundaries: '5' Electric Easement' on the south, '5' Electric Easement' on the east (lower portion), and '5' P.U.E.' on the north. The tree plantings shown on the landscape plan, being placed at or within the property boundary, fall within the 5-foot easement widths. No notes, callouts, or attached documentation on either the landscape plan or site plan reference an executed license agreement obtained from and filed with Austin Energy Public Involvement. The landscape plan's 'IRRIGATION NOTES' section discusses TCEQ Chapter 344 compliance but makes no reference to an easement license agreement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 states that landscaping and irrigation are permissible within electric easements only with a license agreement obtained from and filed with Austin Energy Public Involvement. The checklist specifically requires that plans demonstrate the license agreement has been 'obtained from and filed with' Austin Energy—not to be obtained. The site plan notes in Sheet 9 do not confirm that this agreement exists; instead, note d mentions 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date,' which acknowledges potential future easement constraints but does not address current compliance. Without documented evidence of the executed license agreement, the landscaping plantings shown within the easements cannot be approved. This is a certificate of occupancy hold item per the grouping guidance.
findings.comment: Tree plantings and landscaping are shown within 5-foot electric easements on north, south, and east boundaries without documented evidence of executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement. Provide executed license agreement letter from Austin Energy Public Involvement confirming that landscaping/irrigation within the easement has been 'obtained from and filed with' the City (not 'to be obtained'). Agreement must be attached to site plan submittal prior to approval.

applicableAreas: Tree plantings and landscaping within 5-foot electric easements on property perimeters
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) depicts tree plantings positioned within the 5-foot electric easements running along the north, south, and east property boundaries. Trees are shown with canopy symbols (circles) that extend several feet from the trunk location. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows that these easements run the full length of these property lines. The placement of trees with mature canopies within these easement corridors would create physical obstructions that would prevent unrestricted vehicular access for Austin Energy maintenance personnel and equipment. Easement widths (5 feet) are minimal; tree canopies, trunks, and root systems would occupy much of this width, leaving insufficient space for a maintenance vehicle to traverse the easement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires that landscaping within electric easements be positioned such that it does not restrict 24/7 vehicular access for Austin Energy personnel and equipment. The fundamental purpose of an electric easement is to provide Austin Energy with unrestricted access for construction, operation, maintenance, and repair of electric facilities. Tree plantings shown within the 5-foot easement corridors, with typical canopy spreads of 20-40+ feet (varying by species), would substantially obstruct this required access. Even if a license agreement were in place (which it is not, per EL-5.11), landscaping must be designed to maintain unobstructed access. The current landscape plan does not demonstrate this; trees are shown directly within the easement boundaries.
findings.comment: Tree plantings shown within electric easements would obstruct 24/7 vehicular access required for Austin Energy maintenance. Relocate all trees and landscaping outside the 5-foot electric easement boundaries to maintain unobstructed access corridor, or provide engineer certification that design maintains minimum 12-foot clear width for maintenance vehicle access along entire easement length. Additionally, obtain and file executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement per UCM § 1.10.10.3.

applicableAreas: Wood fencing along eastern and southern property boundaries within 5-foot electric easements
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows fencing lines drawn directly along the eastern and southern property boundaries. These same property boundaries have 5-foot electric easements dedicated to utility use (labeled on Sheet 9 as '5' Electric Easement Vol. 60...' on the east and '5' Elec. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 885...' on the south). The fence lines follow the property boundary, placing them within the 5-foot easement width. The site plan notes describe these as 'Wood Fence' (eastern boundary), consistent with a typical residential privacy fence constructed of wood. Site plan details and notes do not identify these fences as removable, temporary, or specially designed to allow Austin Energy access. Standard residential wood fencing would constitute a permanent, non-removable obstruction within the easement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 explicitly allows removable wooden fences within electric easements under a license agreement if they permit Austin Energy crew and equipment access. However, it prohibits permanent or non-removable fencing. The distinction is critical: 'removable wooden fences' implies temporary structures that can be taken down during maintenance, whereas standard residential wood fences (which appear to be shown on Sheet 9) are permanent structures. The submitted plans do not specify that these fences are removable or designed for Austin Energy access. Additionally, there is no documented license agreement for easement use (per EL-5.11), which would be a prerequisite even for removable fencing. The presence of permanent-appearing wood fences within the easements violates the prohibition on non-removable fencing.
findings.comment: Permanent wood fencing is shown within 5-foot electric easements on eastern and southern property boundaries. UCM § 1.10.10.2 permits only removable wooden fences under license agreement. Either: (1) remove fencing from easement boundaries and relocate outside easement areas, (2) replace with removable fence type with notation indicating removable design allowing Austin Energy access, or (3) obtain executed license agreement from Austin Energy permitting the fence type proposed. Provide details showing fence construction and removability certification if fences will remain within easements.
